text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-weldrs-resolution-20261009/review-astra.md <<'EOF'
## Findings

### 1. [warning] Apply the left-side exclusion before enumerating the posting cross-product
**Location**: `exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder_scoring/blocking.rs:129-137`, `bounded_candidates`

**Finding**: The initial/surname rule indexes excluded legal suffixes with every other suffix, then checks `rule.accepts` only after visiting each pair. A posting whose names all end in `limited` or `ltd` therefore takes quadratic work even though this rule cannot emit any pair. The candidate budget cannot stop this work because the rejected pairs never reach `CandidateSet::insert`.

**Evidence**: For `n` unresolved profiles beginning with the same initial and ending in `limited`, the nested loops visit `n²` combinations and call `accepts` for `n(n-1)/2` pairs. Every call rejects the canonical left endpoint. Such names remain eligible input when they have no accepted company number. Distinct names with distinct three-character prefixes, absent addresses, and distinct blocking keys can reach this rule with no candidates from preceding rules. For example, names of the form `a<distinct Unicode character>x limited` have distinct prefix postings but the same `a\0li` initial/surname posting. With 10,000 profiles this means 100 million loop iterations and no output; increasing the input increases this work quadratically without triggering a budget refusal. This is avoidable work caused by applying a unary predicate after joining.

**Suggestion**: Iterate canonical left endpoints and reject an excluded left once before scanning any right endpoints. For an eligible unresolved left, scan later entries in `all`; for an eligible anchored left, scan later entries in `unresolved`. Keep excluded rows available as right endpoints to preserve the intentionally asymmetric rule. This also removes the per-pair endpoint reordering and unresolved-duplicate branch.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));
